behavior: Raw and optimized interpretation agree with native empty-context metadata/header operations.
Thirteen body limit/error-order cases and three request-header cases compare actual interpreter/native output.
Populated copied results survive source mutation and aliases; tracing stress, verification and reuse poisoning pass.
O1/O2 allocation-failure probes release every partial result; omitted field/header cleanup fails.
POSIX source-stream major-collection control and all-native peer-buffer failure checks remain active.
Response metadata capture rejects allocator failure before callback entry or context installation; existing escaped-child, cancellation and counter-overflow checks remain active.
Generated standard-library documentation agrees with source comments on all six native hosts.

memoryScope.comparison: This is result cleanup and representation evidence, not a timing comparison with C/Rust or a previous fwp revision.
memoryScope.managedResults: Final charged result storage returns to its initialized baseline with collection disabled. Raw connection/stream buffers are outside this budget.
memoryScope.copies: Returned strings, lists and bodies still allocate. Metadata/request construction removes a temporary pointer array; outgoing response normalization removes two temporary string buffers.
memoryScope.rawProtocol: Six header-allocation failures, one buffer resize failure and four size overflows preserve existing storage and release temporary headers. Protocol failure remains exit 102.
limits: Service streams, connections, callbacks and retained contexts are not yet collector-free.
Checked ARC evidence here covers copied values and empty-context public calls, not entire servers.
Allocator metadata, page retention, OpenSSL and total process memory are not measured.
Test binary stack frames include instrumentation and are not a claim about ordinary program speed or total stack use.
